title: California fights "preposterous" Trump admin demand to scrap state broadband laws
author: Jon Brodkin
summary_long: California is accepting $1.42 billion in broadband grant funding from the Trump administration, but the state is not accepting the Trump administration's demand that it stop enforcing a net neutrality law and other telecom regulations. California's stand against the Trump administration could result in multiple legal battles involving the state, federal government, and Internet providers seeking government funds. Although California told the federal government it would accept the money, it is reserving the right to challenge the condition imposed by the US. The state could delay or cancel plans to distribute broadband grants depending on how the process unfolds. Source: arstechnica.com. Date: 2026-11-03. id: bigtech:ukraines drone strikes spur hasty russian plans for undergro:2026-11-03T20:39:55.000Z
title: Ukraine’s drone strikes spur hasty Russian plans for underground data centers
author: Jeremy Hsu
summary_long: Russian tech companies are scrambling to harden and hide their data centers underground after Ukrainian drone strikes damaged facilities housing AI supercomputers and disrupted cloud services for millions of Russian users. Meanwhile, the Kremlin is requiring data center owners to reserve computing capacity for emergency state needs and has even authorized possible use of foreign data centers. These consequences of Russia's war against Ukraine come as the Russian military has bombarded Ukrainian cities with drones and missiles nearly night and day in recent months, along with specifically targeting Ukrainian data centers since late September. But Ukraine has retaliated with its own drone strikes on military and infrastructure targets across Russia, degrading or knocking out data centers operated by Russian tech giant Yandex, the state-owned bank Sberbank, social media site VKontakte, and the Russian Ministry of Finance. id: ai_data:guild guided iterative data collection for imitation learnin:2026-11-03T18:57:35.000Z
title: GUILD: Guided Iterative Data Collection for Imitation Learning
author: Shivin Dass
summary_long: Imitation learning policies in robotics are trained on datasets collected through costly real-world teleoperation. Often, the data-collection process is unguided, relying on the teleoperator's intuition, resulting in data that contributes little to overall policy performance. Recent work has shown that curating such unguided datasets can substantially improve policy performance, but these approaches operate by filtering existing datasets after collection and therefore do not prevent the acquisition of uninformative data. In this work, we propose GUILD, a novel Guided Data Collection (GDC) method that actively reasons about which data should be collected to maximize downstream policy performance. Source: arxiv.org. id: ai_data:harp trainingfree dualprofile agentic communication for llmb:2026-11-03T18:24:20.000Z
title: HARP: Training-Free Dual-Profile Agentic Communication for LLM-Based Recommendation
author: Zhen Tao
summary_long: In LLM-based recommendation, memory acts as a user-level agent in a memory-augmented backbone. Yet users and items remain asymmetric: only the user is given a structured profile; it enters a bandwidth-limited reranker prompt; and it is frozen after warmup. We recast LLM-based recommendation as an agentic-communication process in four stages: BUILD a self-description, TRANSMIT it along the collaborative graph, UNDERSTAND the other side, and SYNC it from the next interaction. This formulation reveals three unresolved communication challenges: the item side never produces a comparable self-description (one-sided BUILD); profile-level signals enter only the bandwidth-limited reranker prompt rather than retrieval, where they would not compete for context tokens (prompt-trapped UNDERSTAND); and the user's description is frozen after warmup with no principled update rule (absent SYNC). Source: arxiv.org. Date: 2026-11-03. Why it matters: outline likely impact on technology, business, or society. What’s next: note near-term developments or signals to watch.

id: ai_data:planteur a croptype segmentation benchmark for tropical regi:2026-11-03T17:10:42.000Z
title: PLANTEUR: A Crop-Type Segmentation Benchmark for Tropical Regions
author: Piper Wolters
summary_long: We introduce PLANTEUR, a benchmark for crop-type mapping from satellite images in the French overseas territories. Building on the PASTIS design, PLANTEUR provides georeferenced and aligned Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, and Landsat-8 sequences with parcel-derived labels spanning six tropical regions and an 8-class label space. We define both a standard test split and a leave-one-island-out protocol to measure cross-territory generalization, and evaluate fully supervised models, linear probes, and fine-tuned foundation models. The benchmark code and data are open source and available on GitHub and Hugging Face. Source: arxiv.org. Date: 2026-11-03. Why it matters: outline likely impact on technology, business, or society.
